prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 4 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 2 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a landscape 16:9 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same moment's world, painted together: the same people, props, weather, light and colour grade in every panel.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 2 is the reference sheet for phone. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: phone exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Anudi is the red mannequin; driver is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one image as a text-free grid, two panels across and two down, read from top left to bottom right. Represent Anudi with a smooth red artist's mannequin and the driver with a smooth blue artist's mannequin, retaining their reference heights and builds. Use soft overcast early-morning daylight, neutral 6000K colour, restrained greys, dusty beige and muted green, with faint amber shop lighting beneath shaded awnings. The asphalt and concrete are already damp; sparse fresh rain appears in the third and fourth panels. Keep the same comfortable right-hand-drive family car throughout. The handbag is structured tan faux leather with short handles, a shoulder strap and brass-coloured fittings; the folding umbrella is navy. The smartphone has an orange back, three rear camera lenses and a transparent cover; its screen contains no readable content. Render the place and props realistically, without lettering, logos, captions, arrows or panel numbers.

Geography: The connected route runs from the rear-left seat of the car to its curb-side rear doorway, then along the narrow pavement toward the office and the compact vending bay farther screen right. The car points screen right at the left curb, and Anudi's exterior route continues left to right without crossing the road. An open kerb drain separates the patched asphalt from the pavement. A weathered concrete boundary wall with a muted-green rectangular patch and an adjacent square utility pole is the connecting landmark: visible through the left window in the car, behind the car at exterior frame left, and progressively farther behind Anudi at frame left in the walking views. The modest office frontage lies ahead of the wall, and the food three-wheeler stands farther along at the pavement's outer edge. Exterior cameras remain streetward of the walking line; the second camera occupies the curb-edge strip of pavement. The vehicle is excluded from the first two panels, appears only partially at the right edge of the third, and becomes fully legible in the fourth, always with its working side concealed.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Seated eye height from the front passenger area, looking diagonally rearward across the cabin; 32mm medium-wide composition holding the rear-left passenger at frame left and the driver in partial profile at the right edge. Background: The rear seat and left side window sit behind the red mannequin. Through that window at frame left are the weathered wall, muted-green patch and square utility pole, with softly resolved Colombo traffic beyond the other glazing. The forward cabin and steering wheel occupy frame right. The red mannequin sits in the rear-left seat at frame left, chest directed toward the car's forward end at screen right and head tilted down toward the orange smartphone in its right hand. Its left hand rests beside the tan handbag on the seat to its left, with the closed navy umbrella laid across the bag. At the right edge, the blue mannequin sits upright with chest and head directed forward toward screen right, both hands touching the steering wheel.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing eye height on the curb-edge strip of pavement, streetward of the walking line, looking obliquely toward the curb-side rear door; 35mm wide composition including the car and the open route toward the office at screen right. Background: The weathered boundary wall, green patch and square pole remain at upper frame left behind the car. The office's concrete frontage and shaded pavement extend across the upper right; patched asphalt and the open kerb drain occupy the lower edge. The vending bay remains beyond the right crop. The car occupies the lower left and centre, its nose pointing screen right and its curb-side rear door still closed, with empty pavement extending toward the office at right. Through the rear side glazing, the red mannequin remains seated with chest toward the car's nose, head lowered toward the smartphone in its right hand, and left hand beside the tan handbag and closed navy umbrella on the seat. Through the front side glazing, the blue mannequin remains seated with chest and head directed screen right and both hands on the steering wheel.
PANEL 3 (row 2, column 1) — Standing eye height from the street side of the walking axis, looking across the pavement; 40mm medium-wide composition from below Anudi's knees, with generous empty space above and toward screen right. Background: The green-patched boundary wall and square pole are now farther back at frame left. The office's weathered concrete frontage fills the central background, while only a narrow section of the food three-wheeler's plain outer body enters at the far right. The same kerb drain runs across the lower frame. The red mannequin is centre-left in a walking stride across the frame toward screen right, chest and head turned together into right-facing three-quarter profile. Its right hand holds the orange smartphone near waist height; the tan handbag hangs from its left forearm, and its lowered left hand holds the navy umbrella fully closed. Sparse rain streaks catch the pale light against the shaded frontage, with ample clear space above the mannequin and only the vehicle's outer edge visible at right.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 2) — Standing eye height from the street side of the same walking axis, looking across the pavement; 35mm wide composition showing Anudi's full figure, the complete open umbrella and the food three-wheeler. Background: The green-patched boundary wall and square pole remain at far frame left, with the office frontage behind the left and middle portions of the pavement. The small dark-green food three-wheeler, with a dark roof and plain enclosed outer side, occupies centre-right; its working side is hidden. The kerb drain continues across the foreground, and the pavement extends beyond the vehicle toward screen right. At frame left, the red mannequin is in full walking profile toward screen right, chest and head aligned with its path alongside the three-wheeler. Its raised left hand holds the fully open navy umbrella overhead, with the tan handbag hanging from the left forearm, while its right hand retains the orange smartphone near its waist. The full canopy and walking figure are clearly separated from the vehicle at centre-right, with sparse rain visible against its darker surfaces.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
